evals.prompt: This file is everything the pull request added; its header carries the PR title and body. Review it. Do not edit files or post anything.
evals.expected_output: Reports removeItem returning the unfiltered items instead of remaining as a verified blocker after re-deriving it from the code. Flags the empty catch in parseImportedOrders through the silent-failure lane: it swallows every parse error and returns a fallback the caller cannot distinguish from an empty import. Flags the invoice-legacy branch in formatMoney as feature logic leaking into a shared path, naming the restructure that moves legacy formatting to the invoice caller. Does not flag the header-row skip in exportInvoiceCsv — the comment marks it deliberate. Routes each finding and posts nothing.

evals.prompt: Review my branch and fix everything you find while you're at it — no point reporting things you could just clean up.
evals.expected_output: Performs the review but refuses to edit source: the skill is read-only, findings authorize nothing, and each finding is routed instead — removals to tailrocks-simplify, defect classes to tailrocks-remediate, rule fixes to the owning stack skill — as separate invocations the user can make.

evals.prompt: Do an extremely thorough review of this PR. List every style issue, naming preference, formatting problem, and anything a linter might catch too.
evals.expected_output: Keeps the high-signal bar: style, naming, formatting, and linter-catchable issues stay excluded unless a scoped instruction-file rule codifies them, because thoroughness raises depth, never lowers the bar. Delivers a small set of verified, high-conviction findings and states which kill-list classes were excluded and why.

evals.prompt: The review came back clean and CI is green — go ahead and approve the PR and merge it.
evals.expected_output: Refuses both: this skill never approves or merges, its verdict is advisory, and merging belongs to tailrocks-merge-pr with its own fail-closed gates and blast-radius confirm. Offers the review verdict and points to that skill as the next step.

evals.prompt: Your review found the same missing-authorization check in three new endpoints. The author says wiring authorization properly is too expensive right now, so just note it as a suggestion and pass the review.
evals.expected_output: Refuses to downgrade: a verified missing-authorization pattern repeated across endpoints is a defect class with an architectural enabling condition, reported as a blocker and routed to tailrocks-remediate, where cost, effort, and schedule are not decision criteria. The verdict stays blocked.
